 Elephant Rumblings: Award Season Continues
 MLB News Roundup
 by Ben Wiley Nov 11, 2026, 3:00 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. 
 Good morning everyone! Happy Wednesday!
 Following Monday’s Rookie of the Year announcements, MLB continued its award season by revealing the 2026 Managers of the Year yesterday.
 Athletics skipper Mark Kotsay was not among the contenders for this prestigious prize. He has yet to lead the team to a winning record or a playoff appearance since succeeding Bob Melvin in 2022. If the 2027 season begins as scheduled and the A’s rise from fourth to first in the American League West standings, Kotsay will likely find himself in the conversation for this award. In contrast, another losing campaign could put his future with the organization in serious doubt.
 Chicago White Sox manager Will Venable deservedly won the AL Manager of the Year award, beating fellow finalists Kevin Cash of the Tampa Bay Rays and Chad Tracy of the Boston Red Sox. Under Venable’s leadership, the White Sox, who lost 100 or more games in each of the previous three seasons, won 84 games and earned an American League Division Series appearance this year.
 In the National League, Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy made history by becoming the first manager to win three consecutive Manager of the Year awards. He received more votes than the other two finalists, Philadelphia Phillies manager Don Mattingly and Atlanta Braves manager Walt Weiss.
 Today, attention shifts to the pitchers. Brewers right-hander Jacob Misiorowski is the favorite for NL Cy Young Award honors after his record-setting season, with New York Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler the favorite for AL Cy Young Award honors.
 Tomorrow, the Most Valuable Player presentations wrap up MLB award season. Like the Cy Young races, the outcomes appear largely predictable, with Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez destined to win their first MVP awards.
 Meanwhile, the general managers meetings in Las Vegas enter day three. There, offseason trade and free agency discussions are beginning to take shape. The meetings represent the first opportunity for the A’s new front-office duo of Taylor Smith and Carlos Castro to meet with executives from around the league and start identifying potential additions to the 2027 roster.
 Despite the looming lockout, the MLB offseason is off to its typically slow start, with no major free-agent signings or trades yet. Should the A’s break the ice by becoming the first team to make a move in free agency? If so, which players would best fit their needs?

 Best of X:
 The introductions continue. Now, it is time for Cam Castro and Taylor Smith to begin reshaping the Athletics roster into one capable of competing for the playoffs next season.
 This reflects Castro’s newness to the organization. After featuring MLB’s worst pitching staff last season, the Athletics desperately need offseason pitching reinforcements to bolster confidence in their rotation and bullpen.
 The A’s Las Vegas ballpark is expected to favor hitters because of its desert location. However, the dome and humidor could help make it more challenging for teams to hit home runs and score runs.
